item.title: Wan'Dale Robinson out for season with ankle injury
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Titans will not have one of their key receivers for the rest of 2026.
item.content:encoded:
The Titans will not have one of their key receivers for the rest of 2026.

Receiver Wan'Dale Robinson is out for the season after being placed on injured reserve this week with an ankle injury, head coach Robert Saleh told reporters in his Wednesday press conference.

Robinson signed with the Titans as a free agent in the offseason, reuniting him with former Giants head coach Brian Daboll, who serves as Tennessee’s offensive coordinator.

In nine games with three starts this season, Robinson caught 38 passes for 272 yards with three touchdowns.

item.title: Todd Monken: Getting flexed into Sunday night is really cool for our players
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: If someone had told you at the beginning of the season that the Week 12 game between the Browns and Raiders would get flexed into Sunday Night Football, you probably would have responded with some healthy skepticism.
item.content:encoded:
If someone had told you at the beginning of the season that the Week 12 game between the Browns and Raiders would get flexed into Sunday Night Football, you probably would have responded with some healthy skepticism.

But with the way the season has unfolded, that's exactly what's happened.

With the Browns at 6-4 and the Raiders at 4-6 — and now starting the league's No. 1 overall pick at quarterback — the two clubs make for one of the most compelling matchups of Thanksgiving weekend that wasn't already in a standalone window.

Browns head coach Todd Monken told reporters on Wednesday that getting flexed is “really cool for our players.”

“I said it at the beginning of the year. I mean, you want to be on Thursday Night, Sunday Night, Monday Night — you want to be flexed, means you’re having a good year,” Monken said, via transcript from the team. “As nice as it is to have a one o’clock schedule every week, I mean, I said that, early in the [year]. I mean, you’re on a trajectory to be fired at some point because you’re at one o’clock every week. So, you’re fighting like hell to get to where you’re on national TV. So, if people are going to watch football, and more importantly than that, an opportunity to get to seven [wins].”

Monken also agreed that it’s a good test for the Browns as a young team.

“I think you earn where you’re at in the present moment, and that only lends itself to what’s in front of you and how important that’s going to become,” Monken said. “You know, getting the bye at 6-4 and putting yourself in position where the rest of the games matter, and especially the one coming up.”

This will be the Browns’ first Sunday night game at home since 2019, which should make for a rowdy atmosphere on the shores of Lake Erie.

“Oh, it’s a huge advantage. Huge advantage,” Monken said of the anticipated environment. “Making it hard for the opposing offense, cadence-wise, being able to function, and making an advantage for us when we’re on offense. I mean, it’s a huge advantage, and it should be playing at home.”

item.title: No practice for Baker Mayfield on Wednesday
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Word on Tuesday was that Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield's outlook for this week's game against the Lions was not promising and Wednesday didn't bring any better news.
item.content:encoded:
Word on Tuesday was that Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield's outlook for this week's game against the Lions was not promising and Wednesday didn't bring any better news.

Mayfield is dealing with a foot injury that had him in a walking boot during the team's bye week and he watched practice in street clothes on Wednesday. The Buccaneers have not made any official determination of his status, but things appear to be trending in the wrong direction.

Jalon Daniels will make his fourth start of the season if Mayfield is unable to play this weekend. The Bucs added Easton Stick to the roster as a third quarterback this week.

Reporters at the open portion of practice also noted that safety Antoine Winfield was not taking part for Tampa.

item.title: Tory Horton's heads up play earns him NFC special teams player of the week
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Late in Sunday's victory over the Raiders, Seahawks receiver Tory Horton made a heads-up play on special teams that helped seal the win.
item.content:encoded:
Late in Sunday's victory over the Raiders, Seahawks receiver Tory Horton made a heads-up play on special teams that helped seal the win.

The league has recognized Horton for his efforts, naming him special teams player of the week.

There was 2:04 remaining in the fourth quarter after Las Vegas narrowed Seattle’s lead to one possession with a 43-yard field goal. The Raiders tried to send the kickoff out of the end zone to preserve the two-minute warning, having just two timeouts left. But Horton leapt up and tipped the ball into the end zone to prevent a touchback. He then signaled for Rashid Shaheed to pick up the football, as he’d stepped out of bounds, to prevent an illegal touch.

Shaheed returned the ball 22 yards, taking the clock down to 1:59.

While the play was flagged for an illegal bat, Las Vegas declined it. A re-kick would have taken more time off the clock.

Quarterback Drew Lock then sealed the victory with a 15-yard run.

This is Horton’s first career player of the week award.

item.title: Cam Little is AFC special teams player of the week for second week in a row
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Jaguars kicker Cam Little turned in another strong game against the Titans last Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Jaguars kicker Cam Little turned in another strong game against the Titans last Sunday.

Little made all four field goals and all four extra points he attempted in Jacksonville's 40-23 win. It was the second straight week that Little made four field goals and the NFL recognized his accomplishment both times.

Little was named the AFC special teams player of the week for the second week in a row. It's the first time that's happened since Cameron Dicker in 2024 and Little joins punter Bryan Barker as the only Jaguars players to pull off the double.

Little is now 18-of-20 on field goals and 29-of-30 on extra points for the season.

item.title: Colts CB Justin Walley named the AFC defensive player of the week
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Colts ended a five-game losing streak with last Sunday's win over the Dolphins and a defensive touchdown played a big role in the 24-22 win.
item.content:encoded:
The Colts ended a five-game losing streak with last Sunday's win over the Dolphins and a defensive touchdown played a big role in the 24-22 win.

Cornerback Justin Walley got home on a blitz deep inside Miami territory and separated Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord from the ball. Defensive tackle Adetomiwa Adebawore recovered the ball for a touchdown.

Walley had five tackles, two tackles for loss and two passes defensed overall in the win. The third-round pick has 40 tackles, two sacks and three forced fumbles to this point in his rookie season.

The NFL named Walley the AFC defensive player of the week on Wednesday. It's the first time a Colt has won the award since early in the 2024 season.

item.title: Jaelan Phillips wins first NFC defensive player of the week award
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Panthers moved into sole possession of first place in the NFC South with their victory over the Saints on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
The Panthers moved into sole possession of first place in the NFC South with their victory over the Saints on Sunday.

Now one of their players has been recognized for his performance in the win.

Edge rusher Jaelan Phillips has been named NFC defensive player of the week.

Phillips had five total tackles with three for loss, a sack, and a fumble recovery that led to a Panthers touchdown in the 20-17 victory.

According to the league, Phillips is the second player in the conference to have three TFLs and a fumble recovery in a single game in 2026.

This is Phillips’ first career defensive player of the week award.

In his first season with Carolina, Phillips has tallied 3.5 sacks, five tackles for loss, and eight QB hits so far in 2026.

item.title: Jahmyr Gibbs wins second NFC offensive player of the week award of the season
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs continued his terrific 2026 season in Sunday's win over the Patriots in Munich.
item.content:encoded:
Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs continued his terrific 2026 season in Sunday's win over the Patriots in Munich.

Now the league has recognized him for his performance in that contest.

Gibbs has been named NFC offensive player of the week.

Gibbs put up 252 yards from scrimmage (153 rushing, 99 receiving) along with two rushing touchdowns in the 35-10 win.

According to the league, Gibbs is just the second player under the age of 25 in NFL history with at least 250 yards from scrimmage and two rushing touchdowns in multiple games, joining Hall of Famer LaDainian Tomlinson. He also scored his 61st and 62nd touchdowns, which puts him past Hall of Famer Terrell Davis for the most touchdowns by a player in his first four seasons in league history.

The 252 yards were the most by a player in a single game so far this season. They were also the second most in an international game in league history.

Gibbs now has five career offensive player of the week awards. He last won it for Week 5 of this year.

Through nine games, Gibbs leads the league with 1,000 rushing yards, 1,384 yards from scrimmage, 11 rushing touchdowns, and 13 total TDs.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is the betting favorite to be the NFL MVP this season and games like the one he had last Sunday are the reason why he's in that spot.
item.content:encoded:
Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is the betting favorite to be the NFL MVP this season and games like the one he had last Sunday are the reason why he's in that spot.

Burrow lit up the Steelers during a 38-18 win that extended Cincinnati's winning streak to five games. Burrow was 35-of-44 for 409 yards and four touchdowns in the victory.

The four touchdowns moved him up to 20 over the course of the winning streak and he leads the league with 27 touchdown passes over the entire season.

The NFL announced on Wednesday that Burrow has been named the AFC offensive player of the week. It's the second time he's won that prize this season and the 10th time in his career.

item.title: Ben Johnson sees Bears' 4.2 yards per carry average as "a deceiving statistic"
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: League wide, NFL teams average 4.2 yards per rushing attempt.
item.content:encoded:
League wide, NFL teams average 4.2 yards per rushing attempt. The Bears also average 4.2 yards per rushing attempt. Bears coach Ben Johnson doesn't much care about that.

What Johnson does care about is that the running game is efficient, and Johnson would like to see better efficiency than he has seen so far from his offense. Johnson noted that an occasional long run can skew the yards per carry average, and if there are too many runs getting stuffed for no gain, that's a problem. On the flip side, a one-yard run will bring down any team's average, but it's a great play if it happens on fourth-and-goal at the 1-yard line.

"I don't see it as bigger chunk runs, necessarily. The yards per carry is a deceiving statistic in a lot of ways," Johnson said. "We run the ball a lot in the red zone, and when you're down there a four-yard carry is really an explosive."

Johnson said what he cares more about is efficiency. Many teams look at running success rate, which means the percentage of runs on which a team gains at least 40 percent of yardage needed on first down, at least 60 percent on second down, or at least 100 percent on third or fourth down. The Bears' success rate this season is 49.2 percent, and Johnson says that's not good enough.

"We go off efficiency, and we're under 50 percent efficient running the ball. We set our bar higher than that. We want to be closer to 55 percent, so we've got some work to do and all our guys know it," Johnson said.

Ultimately, Johnson wants to see rushing first downs and rushing touchdowns. Yards per carry is secondary to that.

item.title: 49ers likely won't cut Brandon Aiyuk until they have to
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: With a roster exemption that lasts until November 24 and with no requirement to pay him a penny until the exemption expires, the 49ers have shown no inclination to release receiver Brandon Aiyuk until they absolutely have to.
item.content:encoded:
With a roster exemption that lasts until November 24 and with no requirement to pay him a penny until the exemption expires, the 49ers have shown no inclination to release receiver Brandon Aiyuk until they absolutely have to.

Nine days since Aiyuk was reinstated from the reserve/left squad list, the 49ers haven't cut him. At this point, with only six days to go, the 49ers surely will kick the can as long as they can.

They gain nothing from delaying Aiyuk's return, other than the relatively minor strategic advantage of keeping him away from a competitor. With all signs pointing to Aiyuk landing in Washington, he's no threat to San Francisco's playoff interests.

Of course, the receiver-needy Rams could get involved. Or perhaps the Vikings, who are currently without Jordan Addison. Or maybe the Seahawks, who don't have a clear No. 2 option behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

If the 49ers are simply squatting on Aiyuk out of spite, that's a bush-league move that creates bad karma. Let the guy get back in the league. They apparently still have the ability to pursue upwards of $13 million in bonus money from him; use that process as the vehicle for getting a pound of flesh.

Regardless, the 49ers apparently won't be letting him go until the exemption expires. At that point, he'll pass through waivers, his contract won't be claimed, and he'll become a free agent.

item.title: Vikings WR Jauan Jennings prepare to face his former team
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Sunday night's game in Mexico City between the Vikings and 49ers has multiple interesting subplots.
item.content:encoded:
Sunday night's game in Mexico City between the Vikings and 49ers has multiple interesting subplots. One relates to a player who had spent his entire career with the 49ers before signing with Minnesota.

Jauan Jennings is in his first season as a Viking. In six games with two starts, he has only six catches for 54 yards.

And there was a strong possibility of a trade back to the 49ers. He ultimately decided to stay where he was.

The Vikings will need him on Sunday night, especially with receiver Jordan Addison out due to a thumb injury.

“With us being down Jordan Addison, we’re gonna need him to make some plays in the pass game," coach Kevin O'Connell said Tuesday on KFAN.

Jennings didn't play in Week 10 at Green Bay due to a calf injury.

During five seasons with the 49ers, Jennings caught 210 passes for 2,581 yards and 22 touchdowns in 75 regular-season games. He also had 23 catches for 289 yards and a touchdown in 11 postseason games — including four catches for 42 yards and a touchdownand a touchdown pass in Super Bowl LIX.

Without Addison, Jennings could get more opportunities. And he will surely have a little extra incentive to show his former team that they should have kept him around.

item.title: Report: Mike Pettine takes over as Cowboys' defensive play-caller
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Christian Parker will remain the defensive coordinator.
item.content:encoded:
This one was inevitable, perhaps from the moment Mike Pettine arrived last month as an assistant.

Via ESPN, Pettine will be taking over as the play-caller for the Dallas Cowboys defense.

Pettine supplants defensive coordinator Christian Parker, a Pettine protege who is in his first year as the coach in charge of an NFL defense. Parker will remain the team's defensive coordinator.

It was obvious that something was coming. Sunday's 46-40 loss to the 49ers included an embarrassing performance from the defense, highlighted by multiple players running the wrong way when receiver Deebo Samuel rumbled 70 yards for a rushing touchdown.

Some would say Pettine is part of the problem, given that he has been there for multiple weeks. Short of firing everyone and hiring someone off the street, however, there's not much that can be done right now.

The first test comes on Sunday, when the Cowboys host the one-win Titans. Four days later, Dallas faces the two-win Eagles. If the Cowboys don't win both, they'll likely be de facto done for 2026.

item.title: For the Seahawks this year, Drew Lock's numbers blow Sam Darnold's away
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: When Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald confirmed that Sam Darnold will start in Week 12 against the 49ers, assuming he is medically cleared, it was no surprise: The Seahawks signed Darnold to a three-year, $100 million contract last year and won the Super Bowl with Darnold at the helm.
item.content:encoded:
When Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald confirmed that Sam Darnold will start in Week 12 against the 49ers, assuming he is medically cleared, it was no surprise: The Seahawks signed Darnold to a three-year, $100 million contract last year and won the Super Bowl with Darnold at the helm. Quarterbacks like that don't often get benched.

But Drew Lock has made it reasonable to question whether Darnold should get benched.

That's because Lock has played three full games, and most of a fourth, while Darnold has missed time with injuries this season. And Lock hasn't just been better than Darnold. Lock has been so much better that there's no comparison between the two.

The Seahawks are 4-0 in the games when Lock was their primary quarterback. They're 2-4 in the games with Darnold as the primary quarterback.

Of the 37 NFL quarterbacks who have thrown at least 90 passes this season, Lock ranks first with a passer rating of 125.6. Darnold ranks 31st with a passer rating of 79.5.

Lock has still not thrown an interception this season. Darnold has thrown nine.

Lock has completed 73.1 percent of his passes. Darnold has completed 60.2 percent.

Lock is averaging 9.0 yards per pass. Darnold is averaging 7.0 yards per pass.

Lock has been sacked on 5.1 percent of his dropbacks. Darnold has been sacked on 7.5 percent of his dropbacks.

With seven games left in the season, the 6-4 Seahawks are going to have a battle to get back to the playoffs. Macdonald believes Darnold is the best quarterback for the job. The numbers call that into question.

item.title: PFT's Week 11 2026 NFL power rankings
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Bills remain on top.
item.content:encoded:
1. Bills (last week No. 1; 8-1): For three straight weeks, a sluggish start turns into an easy win.

2. Jaguars (No. 2; 7-2): Parker Washington is playing his way into the franchise tag.

3. 49ers (No. 3; 8-1): The defense is going to need to perform better against the Vikings.

4. Broncos (No. 4; 7-2): The next time the Chargers play the Broncos, Sean Payton will tell Jim Harbaugh to stick his "loophole" up his poophole.

5. Bears (No. 5; 7-2): They can't afford to overlook the Saints, four days before a showdown with the Lions.

6. Chiefs (No. 6; 7-2): There's nothing wrong with Patrick Mahomes's elbow.

7. Bengals (No. 8; 7-2): Joe Burrow was right about feeling 2019 LSU vibes.

8. Seahawks (No. 9; 6-4): "Take your time, Sam."

9. Lions (No. 10; 7-2): Dealing with significant defensive injuries has become part of their normal.

10. Vikings (No. 12; 7-2): The "story being written" could lead to a Pulitzer Prize shaped like a Super Bowl trophy.

11. Steelers (No. 7; 6-3): They're not ready to compete with the best teams in the conference.

12. Rams (No. 15; 6-4): Can they keep winning without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams?

13. Packers (No. 11; 6-4): They desperately need a running game.

14. Browns (No. 16; 6-4): The playoffs are anything but a pipe dream.

15. Giants (No. 13; 5-3-1): They'll need the extra days to get ready for the Jaguars.

16. Patriots (No. 14; 5-5): It feels like the wheels are coming off.

17. Panthers (No. 22; 4-5): Feed Chuba.

18. Raiders (No. 17; 4-6): Fernando Mendoza looks the part, but they possibly could have beaten the Seahawks with Kirk Cousins.

19. Buccaneers (No. 18; 3-6): They could catch the Lions napping on Sunday.

20. Ravens (No. 19; 4-6): They won't have to worry about Lamar Jackson making it back for a playoff push.

21. Commanders (No. 26; 3-5-1): When the dust settles on the season, they could be the NFC East champions.

22. Texans (No. 20; 3-6): Last year, the defense was good enough to win games on its own. This year, the defense is bad enough to lose games on its own.

23. Saints (No. 21; 3-6): They need to stop sleepwalking through the first 30 minutes.

24. Cowboys (No. 25; 4-6): The defense has gotten worse, not better.

25. Cardinals (No. 23; 3-7): They should hire Rex Ryan solely for the entertainment value.

26. Falcons (No. 24; 3-7): How long until Andy Dalton gets a shot?

item.title: C.J. Stroud: "There's still a lot of ball to be played"
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: With Sunday's loss to the Browns, the Texans have fallen to 3-6 on the season.
item.content:encoded:
With Sunday's loss to the Browns, the Texans have fallen to 3-6 on the season.

At this point, Houston will have to rip off several wins in a row to have a chance at the postseason.

Quarterback C.J. Stroud is remaining optimistic.

“There's still a lot of ball to be played, if I can remember I think we'll be fine,” Stroud said on Tuesday, via transcript from the team. “It's not perfection that is what's needed, but it's a chase of excellence from everybody. Me and [ Will Anderson Jr.], we try to set the standard every day for everybody in the building to look at us and be like, 'Hey, those are two guys that I want to follow after,' and it's up to us to keep that standard going.

“It doesn't mean because you lose a couple games that everything got to switch or change. There's a lot of ball to be played left, so we're still excited about what's coming next.”

So Stroud remains motivated and wants that attitude to permeate throughout the team.

"What else are we going to do? Cry about it and hold our heads down? Woe is us, woe is this team? I don't believe in that,” Stroud said. “It sucks, yeah, I'm not the happiest camper, but I think the motivated me is one of the best me's that I've seen.

“I think even as this team, the motivated Texans is a scary team. It's up to us. We don't need anybody else. That's my message to the guys. We don't need anybody else to have faith in us or to think that we can do this or can't do this. It doesn't really matter. We're the ones on the field making plays and we have the opportunity. Everybody can have an opinion, but when you have the opportunity, you've got to go and do it and I think it just starts one thing at a time."

item.title: Seahawks owner Vinod Khosla: "We’re very happy with both the team and the location right now"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: A pattern has emerged during the early months of Vinod Khosla's ownership of the Seahawks.
item.content:encoded:
A pattern has emerged during the early months of Vinod Khosla's ownership of the Seahawks.

First, he'll make a less-than-unequivocal comment about the future of the team in Seattle. Two, people will hear his words and repeat them. Three, he will complain about that.

Most recently, Khosla was asked directly during an appearance on CNBC whether he'd consider moving the team.

"I’ve not made any plans or even discussed -- I know the press like to make a big deal of it," Khosla said, via Sports Business Journal. "We’re very happy with both the team and the location right now."

And there it is. "Right now." Why add "right now"? Just end the sentence at "location."

The same thing happened last month, when Khosla was interviewed by Axios. Asked point-blank whether he'd make a commitment to keeping the Seahawks in Seattle over the long term, Khosla said, “I will never say never. Will this team be in Seattle 500 years from now? But I have no current plans to change anything about the team, including the coach, president, operation or Lumen Field. It all functions well.”

It's not difficult (although apparently it is). The question is simple. Will you move from Seattle?

While there's an element of taxpayer-funding leverage that arises regarding future stadium renovations and/or construction in Seattle, there's a way to answer the question that doesn't sacrifice future bargaining power.

"We have every intention to remain in Seattle" is the easiest reply. With no further elaboration or explanation.

Frankly, his latest comments are more ominous than his response to the Axios question. Beyond the fact that he now knows anything he says will be repeated (indeed, he prefaced his response by saying "the press like to make a big deal of it"), Khosla added the ultimate caveat that will cause local consternation.

"Right now."

Right now isn't "500 years from now." Right now is subject to change. Because right now applies only to — wait for it — right now.

Right now is later from the last time I typed "right now."

Here's what Khosla should do: Write a check right now to someone who will give him a script to recite whenever he's asked that question in the future right now.

item.title: NFL flexes Raiders-Browns to Sunday night in Week 12
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Originally scheduled for SNF, Patriots-Chargers moves to 4:05 p.m. on CBS.
item.content:encoded:
Reigning No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza will make his primetime debut sooner than originally scheduled.

The NFL announced on Tuesday that it has flexed the Week 12 matchup between the Raiders and Browns in Cleveland to Sunday Night Football.

The two teams were originally scheduled to kick off at 1 p.m. with Patriots-Chargers scheduled for Sunday night.

New England and Los Angeles will now kick off at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS. The matchup between the Titans and Jaguars in Jacksonville has also been moved to 1 p.m. on Fox.

Currently 4-6, the Raiders will have a chance to be 5-6 when they come to Cleveland as they’ll take on the Broncos in Denver this weekend. It will be Mendoza’s second career start, with the matchup against the AFC North foe in Week 12 his third.

The surprising 6-4 Browns got back in the win column with a 27-24 victory over the Texans on Sunday. All six of Cleveland’s victories this season have come via a fourth-quarter comeback.

The Browns are on their bye in Week 11.

Cleveland and Las Vegas faced one another last season, with the Browns coming away with a 24-10 victory in Week 12. It was the first start of Shedeur Sanders’ career, though he is now serving as the backup to Deshaun Watson.

This will be the first Sunday night game in Cleveland since 2019, when the Browns fell to the Rams in Week 3.

item.title: Dan Campbell: I'm not telling players to stop celebrating because of Aidan Hutchinson's injury
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Hutchinson tore his ACL while celebrating a sack.
item.content:encoded:
Lions head coach Dan Campbell isn't going to tell his players to stop celebrating in the wake of defensive end Aidan Hutchinson's torn ACL.

Hutchinson will miss the rest of the season after injuring his right knee while celebrating a sack of Drake Maye in Sunday's game. Hutchinson jumped in the air and immediately grabbed his right knee after suffering the injury when he landed back on the turf in Munich.

During an appearance on 97.1 The Ticket on Tuesday, Campbell called the injury "one of those things that happened" and that "this game is built off of emotion" that he doesn't want to take away from his players.

"I hate it, I know he hates it. But I mean, the number of moves that I’ve seen Hutch make and the number of plyometrics, explosive movements, the spins, the one leg lateral movements, lateral balances, I’m just like, it was one of those things, man," Campbell said. "I hate it. I think we all understand what it is, and let’s be smart, but no, I’m not gonna say, 'Nobody celebrates anymore.'"

Campbell recounted a story from his own playing days when he tore his biceps while celebrating a play and that didn't lead him to make celebration avoidance a rule for the Lions when he got the job. That doesn't make Hutchinson's injury any easier for the Lions to deal with, but it makes his response to questions about the advice he'll give in the future easier to understand.

item.title: Jahmyr Gibbs is on pace to break the NFL record for yards from scrimmage in a season
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The current record belongs to Chris Johnson, who had 2,509 yards for the Titans in 2009.
item.content:encoded:
Detroit's Jahmyr Gibbs hasn't just been the most productive running back in the NFL this season. He may produce more yardage than any player in NFL history this season.

Through nine games this season, Gibbs has an NFL-high 1,000 rushing yards. Gibbs also has 384 receiving yards. That total of 1,384 yards from scrimmage leads the league, and with an average of 153.8 yards per game, Gibbs is on pace total 2,614 yards from scrimmage over a 17-game season.

That would break the NFL record, held by Chris Johnson of the Titans, who totaled 2,509 yards from scrimmage (2,006 rushing yards and 503 receiving yards) in 2009.

Gibbs has touched the ball an NFL-high 240 times this season, combining 199 carries and 41 catches. With that kind of workload, the biggest concern for the Lions will be whether he can stay healthy for 17 regular-season games and, the Lions hope, some playoff games after that.

But given how well Gibbs is playing, it would be hard for Dan Campbell and the Lions' coaching staff to reduce his workload. He's having a special season. He's halfway to one of the greatest seasons any running back has ever had.

item.title: Brian Flores: Vikings plan to rotate players in order to deal with altitude in Mexico City
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The 49ers are spending the week in Colorado in order to acclimate to the altitude at which their Week 11 game in Mexico City will be played.
item.content:encoded:
The 49ers are spending the week in Colorado in order to acclimate to the altitude at which their Week 11 game in Mexico City will be played. The Vikings are not.

But the Vikings have a plan for ensuring that their players are ready for the conditions.

"It's a tough place to play," Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores told reporters on Tuesday regarding the game in Mexico. "I think it's certainly taxing, you know, I think you're — I think as a staff, we're already talking about, 'Hey, we're gonna have to rotate these guys and get, you know, everybody's gonna have to be ready to play.' And so, yeah, I mean, it's certainly something that we're going to have to deal with.

"But there's always, you know, elements that we're dealing with, whether it's cold or rain or things like that. Obviously, we're indoors, so we don't deal with much of that. But that's the environment we're gonna be in. I think we prepare them to play in that environment, but I'm not gonna be silly and say, 'Hey, everybody, hey, you've got to go in there for 12 straight plays.' I mean, we're not doing that.

"So we'll have rotations, we'll have a plan in place. Inevitably, we're gonna have to fight through some of that. It's not gonna be your average game where, you know, altitude, you just have — you literally have less oxygen. So we've got to do a great job as a staff of making sure — watching guys, and making sure we got guys in and out, you know, as much as we can."

His broader message to the defense is clear: "We're gonna need everybody."

Regardless of the plan to rotate players, the question becomes whether the 49ers will be able to rely more heavily on their best players because they're properly acclimated to the thinner air. The Vikings are choosing a different strategy, and it's going to create an obvious apples to apples comparison between the approaches that the two teams have taken — especially if the 49ers players seem to be fresh and the Vikings players seem to be gassed.

item.title: Gardner Minshew had surgery to repair torn ligament in throwing elbow
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew has had surgery to repair the elbow injury that ended his season.
item.content:encoded:
Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew has had surgery to repair the elbow injury that ended his season.

Minshew had the surgery on his right ulnar collateral ligament on Monday and is expected to make a full recovery, according to ESPN.

Although tearing the UCL is a famously brutal injury for baseball pitchers that necessitated the development of the Tommy John surgery procedure, it tends not to be as severe for the throwing motion of a quarterback. Brock Purdy tore his UCL in the 49ers' playoff loss in January of 2023, had surgery to repair it in March, and was healthy enough to play the full season and lead the 49ers to the Super Bowl the next year.

Minshew, who will be a free agent in March, should be healthy enough to sign with some team and play in 2027. Where he'll be playing remains a question.

item.title: Report: Aidan Hutchinson has torn ACL but no additional damage
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson received a bit of good news after additional testing on his right knee.
item.content:encoded:
Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson received a bit of good news after additional testing on his right knee.

Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reports that, while Hutchinson will miss the rest of the season with a torn ACL, he has no other significant damage.

Initial reports indicated the Lions feared Hutchinson "probably" had additional damage in his knee, specifically his meniscus.

Hutchinson and Patriots quarterback Drake Maye were both injured on Hutchinson's third-down sack of Maye with 9:28 left in the first quarter. Maye injured his ankle on the play, and the injury could be season-ending. Hutchinson injured his knee on the celebration afterward.

Walt Anderson, the NFL’s officiating rules analyst, said through a league spokesman that Hutchinson's tackle was not an illegal hip drop.

This marks the second time in three seasons that Hutchinson's season will end early. He finishes 2026 with six sacks.

item.title: When Brian Flores defenses face Kyle Shanahan offenses, Flores is 5-0
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Teams with Flores as a head coach or defensive assistant have played against teams with Shanahan as a head coach or offensive assistant five times, and Flores is 5-0.
item.content:encoded:
Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores will face off with 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan on Sunday night in Mexico City, and if history is any guide, Flores has the advantage.

Teams with Flores as a head coach or defensive assistant have played against teams with Shanahan as a head coach or offensive assistant five times, and Flores is 5-0.

Since becoming defensive coordinator of the Vikings, Flores has coached against Shanahan's 49ers twice, with Flores' team coming out on top both times. In 2023, the Vikings beat the 49ers 22-17. In 2024, the Vikings beat the 49ers 23-17.

Flores and Shanahan coached against each other as head coaches once, in 2020, when Flores' Dolphins beat Shanahan's 49ers 43-17.

The most famous game with Flores and Shanahan on opposite sides came in Super Bowl LI, when Flores was linebackers coach for the Patriots and Shanahan was offensive coordinator for the Falcons. Shanahan's Falcons jumped out to a 28-3 lead, only to have Flores' Patriots come back and win 34-28 in overtime.

And in 2011, New England beat Washington 34-27 when Flores was a defensive assistant in New England and Shanahan was offensive coordinator in Washington.

Shanahan was once on a coaching staff that got a win against a team with Flores on the staff, in the final game of the 2009 season, when the Patriots had already clinched their playoff spot, rested starters and lost to a Texans team with Shanahan as offensive coordinator. But Flores was a special teams assistant, not a defensive assistant, on that Patriots team, so that game wasn't a Flores defense vs. Shanahan offense competition.

When it's Flores coaching defense against Shanahan coaching offense, the result has been the same across different teams and in different coaching roles: Flores has five wins and Shanahan has none.

item.title: Dan Campbell says Buccaneers are better than their record says they are
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Lions head coach Dan Campbell played in the NFL for Bill Parcells, who liked to say, "You are what your record says you are."
item.content:encoded:
Lions head coach Dan Campbell played in the NFL for Bill Parcells, who liked to say, "You are what your record says you are." That's not how Campbell views this week's opponent.

With the Lions preparing to face the 3-6 Buccaneers on Sunday, Campbell said he thinks they're a much better team than that record suggests, and he noted that Tampa Bay is only a game out of first place in the NFC South.

"It's a physical team. These guys play with violence. Todd Bowles always does a great job. Their record is not indicative of the type of team they are. They're in the hunt for the South. So we know what we have in front of us," Campbell said.

In the NFL's worst division, the Buccaneers have a real chance to be a playoff team, and Sunday's game could even be a playoff preview. That's how Campbell wants his players to view it: As a game against a playoff opponent, not against a team that's 3-6.

item.title: Caleb Williams remains frustrated with four interception game
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: In his last game, Caleb Williams threw four interceptions.
item.content:encoded:
In his last game, Caleb Williams threw four interceptions. The quarterback has not had a chance to truly put it behind him yet as the Bears had an off week in Week 10.

He called two of the picks "funky" and a third "a bad decision."

"The biggest thing is, the frustration comes from the feeling of, for me, personally, I always don't want to let my teammates down," Williams said, via Courtney Cronin of ESPN. "That’s always big for me. And in that situation, in those situations, I feel like I did. And so, that's the frustrating part that lingers."

Williams had thrown four total interceptions in the 11 games before the Bucs game, dating to Nov. 28, 2025. He had never thrown more than two in a game.

"He's playing fast right now," Johnson said. "He's got a great approach. He's doing a good job downloading the game plan. We don't feel like we're hindered in any way as a coaching staff from the schematics of what we're able to put in, the details, the alerts. He's just able to digest a lot more. He's seeing coverage really well with where his eyes should be tied into his feet also. So, we're really encouraged with where he's at. We've just got to continue to push that envelope and see how far it will take us."

During his break, Williams' close friend, Cubs outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong, won the National League MVP award. Williams' odds to win NFL MVP are +3500.

Williams was asked whether Chicago is big enough to handle two MVPs.

"Damn right," he said, smiling.

item.title: 49ers-Cowboys cranks out 27.13 million viewers
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Fox's Sunday tripleheader culminated in the national telecast of the 8-1 49ers at the record-doesn't-matter Cowboys.
item.content:encoded:
Fox's Sunday tripleheader culminated in the national telecast of the 8-1 49ers at the record-doesn't-matter Cowboys.

As expected, it delivered.

On average, 27.13 million watched the 46-40 barnburner, which ultimately underscored the fact that: (1) the 49ers are elite; and (2) the old "Doomsday Defense" nickname has a much different meaning now.

The performance of the game reconfirms the fact that 4:25 p.m. ET has become the most valuable weekly window. It currently rotates between CBS and FOX, with multiple simultaneous games per year.

It's hard not to imagine the NFL considering breaking that window away from the standard Sunday afternoon packages and selling it to one network. Given the size of the audiences, it would be the most lucrative package the NFL could offer.

This week, the NFL moved Steelers-Eagles from the late-afternoon window on CBS and shifted Jaguars-Giants into the spot. Raiders-Broncos also starts at 4:25 p.m. ET.
